_note: ThusoIQ Core's routes are called by engines, not people: the bus, the closed loop, the alert router, the protocol registry, the permission check and the audit export. Wave 2 contract; Wave 3 build. Nothing here runs yet.

refusals.statement: An engine publishes only the events it owns.
refusals.why: A second publisher is a second source of truth for the same fact.

refusals.statement: A loop is not closed without an outcome.
refusals.why: The closed loop exists so that no concern is done until what happened is recorded.

refusals.statement: A protocol is ratified with a named role and a date.
refusals.why: A recommendation cites the board's authority; the registry must say whose it was and when.

refusals.statement: A withdrawn event version is neither published nor subscribed to.
refusals.why: Its correction is the next version.

ownIds.why: The id the bus assigns to an event it accepted.

routes.summary: Publish an event to the bus.

request.why: The envelope and payload, in the frozen shape.

refusals.statement: An engine publishes only the events it owns.
refusals.why: Ownership is checked against the certificate's engine id, not the payload's claim.

refusals.statement: That event version is withdrawn and is not published.
refusals.why: A withdrawn version has no subscribers and its correction is the next version.

refusals.statement: The event carries a field the bus refuses.
refusals.why: The never-lists in packages/catalog/events.json are enforced at publish as well as at build.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Publishing carries another engine's event; Core adds none of its own.

capabilityNamed.what: Event bus with versioned JSON event contracts

routes.summary: Open a concern with an owner, a deadline and a fallback.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The engine the concern came from.
Who owns it when the deadline passes.

refusals.why: A concern with no owner is one nobody is waiting on.

refusals.statement: Every concern has a fallback for when its owner does not answer.
refusals.why: Unacknowledged items escalate automatically, or they wait for somebody to notice.

routes.summary: The owner takes the concern on.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.

refusals.why: Acknowledging a closed loop would reopen it without an outcome.

routes.summary: Move the concern to its fallback.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.

refusals.statement: There is nobody left on the rota to escalate to.
refusals.why: The desk is told, rather than the loop quietly stopping.

routes.summary: Close the concern with its outcome.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.

refusals.statement: A loop is not closed without an outcome.
refusals.why: An outcome-less close is a loop closed by pressing a button.

routes.summary: Raise an alert: routed by rung, de-duplicated, suppressible, snoozed only with a reason.

request.why: The rung on the escalation ladder.
The record entry the concern is about. Never the reading itself.
Two alerts with one key are one alert.

response.why: Whether a suppression window absorbed it.

refusals.statement: An alert carries a reference to the record entry, never a reading.
refusals.why: Alerts are copied into digests and escalated to people outside the care team.

refusals.statement: An alert is snoozed only with a reason.
refusals.why: A silent snooze is how an alert is lost.

capabilityNamed.what: Deduplication, suppression windows, severity tiers, snooze-with-reason

routes.summary: Read a protocol version from the registry.

refusals.statement: No such protocol version is registered.
refusals.why: A version the registry does not hold cannot be cited.

capabilityNamed.what: Protocol registry with versioning and board sign-off

routes.summary: The Medical Director ratifies a protocol version.

request.why: The day of the board's sign-off.

refusals.statement: A protocol is ratified with a named role and a date.
refusals.why: The registry records whose authority a recommendation borrows.

refusals.statement: A draft with no content cannot be ratified.
refusals.why: The board ratifies words; a name and a number are not a protocol.

routes.summary: Check role × scope × purpose before an engine acts.

refusals.statement: That role is not in the scope matrix.
refusals.why: An unknown role is refused, never defaulted.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A check changes nothing; the gate that acts on it writes the audit entry.

capabilityNamed.what: Role and scope matrix enforced on every API

routes.summary: Export the append-only audit trail for a period.

response.why: Whether the chain verified across the period.

refusals.statement: An export covers a bounded period.
refusals.why: An unbounded export is a copy of the whole trail in one place.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: An export is itself an audit entry in the chain it exports.
